findings.summary: Checked-in synthetic Source artifacts retain exact SHA-256 bindings, and every supporting EvidenceLink reproducibly resolves its unique locator to the revision's source-native raw expression and atomic Claim statement.

Spatial refinement rejects changes to calendar/normalization, inclusivity, qualifiers and alternatives in its valid-time semantic envelope, while revision-local basis_claim_refs may change without being mistaken for temporal meaning.
The validator enforces exactly one series per atomic subject_ref/target_key pair, target-key/dimension compatibility and dimension-appropriate revision value families.

Valid time and record time remain distinct; deterministic replay, correction, unresolved alternatives, withdrawal, separate ecological world states, fuzzy ranges and geometry-null unknown routes preserve the intended semantic scenarios.

The documented Drive-to-curation-to-GitHub-to-controlled-projection path and minimum-fidelity stop rule remain coherent; Gate D, public runtime, empty Airtable historical-write authority, project_state.json and frozen #329/#330/Gate C packages remain unchanged.

Temporal refine now rejects a changed calendar/normalization profile and every primary or alternative member outside all predecessor members; the prior 1600-01-01 alternative mutation is fail-closed, and revision-local basis_claim_refs additions remain accepted.

Temporal refinement does not implement strict narrowing of the full possible-set union or the contract's open-bound cases. A controlled full-package mutation with recomputed locks was accepted when predecessor and child both retained the same unknown alternative: although the primary interval narrowed, both unions remained universal, so refine was false. Conversely, a finite child contained by an open-start predecessor was rejected, as were valid same-bound narrowing by exclusivity or finer supported precision, because qualifier handling and the final strictness check operate on primary finite dates only.

The round-3 calendar/profile and outside-alternative defect is resolved, but full possible-set strictness and open-bound refinement remain semantically incomplete, so this candidate is not READY.
